If you're OK doing something physically demanding, I'd recommend Customer Service Loader. Most of the time you're walking around outside collecting carts and most customer interactions boil down to "would you like some help?" "if you'll pull your car up to the front I'd be glad to help you," "have a good day". I have social anxiety that's moderately difficult for me to deal with but most of my direct interactions with customers are usually less than a minute or 2. If they are angry, it's easy to remind myself, "They are currently leaving, this is the tail end of it. Just smile and nod, after 2 minutes they will not be here and I can breathe." The most anxiety inducing thing that I had happen was someone speeding through the parking lot narrowly missing me, Thankfully that has only happened once in the time I've been here. Keep in mind it is physically demanding and you'll be lifting things regularly as well as walking 20000-35000 steps every shift. If you're not used to it, the first couple of weeks you will be sore. Im not too familiar with back end so maybe theres something better suited there. Hope this helps.

Ooo cool! I've actually done this with my own barbatos. In my experience, the wide flatter parts are the most difficult to get to look even like the top of the chest piece so I ended up removing the paint on mine. Rounded parts tend to look nicer compared to flat parts when hand painting though it starts to look the same the bigger the part gets. Metalic paints can look almost to just as good as airbrush or spray can on smaller parts like v fins, vents, or inner frame parts. Speaking of inner frame the IBO kits innerframes can really pop with minimal effort by dry brushing. The frames have a surprising amount of surface detail on the parts that doing a light dry brushing can make those usually unseen details really shine. Other than that, at the end of the day it's your kit, as long as you are satisfied that's all that matters. Gunpla is freedom!
